problems.title: Display Capture black screen
symptoms: Preview or stream output is entirely black
No picture after adding a Display Capture source
causes: OBS is not running as administrator, so it cannot capture the desktop
The hardware-accelerated capture method is incompatible on Windows 11
Conflicts with hardware acceleration in Chrome/Discord and similar apps

steps.title: Run OBS as administrator
steps.detail: Right-click the OBS shortcut → Run as administrator; to make it permanent, check "Run this program as an administrator" under Properties → Compatibility.

steps.title: Switch to Windows Graphics Capture on Windows 11
steps.detail: Double-click the Display Capture source → Properties → set Capture Method to "Windows Graphics Capture (WGC)", which is most stable on Win11.

steps.title: Turn off hardware acceleration in conflicting apps
steps.detail: Chrome: Settings → System → turn off "Use hardware acceleration"; Discord: Settings → Advanced → turn off hardware acceleration, then restart OBS.

tips: Display Capture is the heaviest option; avoid it when possible and prefer Game/Window Capture
Close sensitive windows and notifications before capturing to avoid leaking private information

problems.title: Game Capture black screen
symptoms: Fullscreen games show a black screen in OBS
The game is running but the Game Capture source is black
causes: OBS and the game have mismatched privileges (both must run as administrator)
OBS and the game use different GPUs (dual graphics)
Anti-cheat engines (Vanguard/BattlEye/EAC) block injection
Wrong capture mode selected

steps.title: Run OBS as administrator
steps.detail: Modern games (Valorant, COD, and similar) require elevation. Right-click the OBS shortcut → Run as administrator.

steps.title: Switch the capture mode to "Capture specific window"
steps.detail: Delete the old Game Capture source and add Game Capture again → set Mode to "Capture specific window" → select the game exe. More reliable than "Capture any fullscreen application".

steps.title: Enable the anti-cheat compatibility hook
steps.detail: In the Game Capture properties, check "Use anti-cheat compatibility hook" (required for BattlEye/EAC/Vanguard); if it is still black, uncheck and recheck it to refresh.

steps.title: Unify the GPU (dual-graphics laptops)
steps.detail: NVIDIA Control Panel → Manage 3D settings → Program Settings → add OBS → set Preferred graphics processor to "High-performance NVIDIA processor" to match the game.

tips: As a last resort, fall back to Window Capture (Windows 10 1903+ method)
Display Capture is the very last resort, but it exposes your entire desktop

problems.title: Window Capture fails to capture / black screen
symptoms: Window Capture source is black or blank
Wrong window is captured or it crashes
The picture suddenly goes black mid-stream/recording and recovers after restarting the capture source (intermittent)
causes: Cannot capture after the window is minimized
An incompatible capture method is used (Vulkan/Microsoft Store apps)
The source is disabled (eye icon off)
The target app switches render modes or enters exclusive fullscreen mid-session, invalidating the capture handle (a common cause of sudden intermittent black screens)
A GPU driver reset or sudden spike in GPU load makes Windows Graphics Capture (WGC) drop frames intermittently
The target app enables hardware acceleration, so its window content uses a separate swap chain that conflicts with the capture session

steps.title: Check that the source is not disabled and the window is not minimized
steps.detail: Check that the eye icon for the source is on in the Sources list; the window must not be minimized to the taskbar.

steps.title: Switch the capture method
steps.detail: Double-click the Window Capture source → change Capture Method from "Automatic" to "Windows 10 (1903 and newer)", which works better for most modern apps.

steps.title: Fall back to Game Capture for Microsoft Store/UWP apps
steps.detail: Some UWP or Vulkan programs reject standard Window Capture; switch to Game Capture or Display Capture.

steps.title: Refresh the capture source first when the screen suddenly goes black
steps.detail: When it suddenly goes black, right-click the source → Properties → reselect the target window and click OK (or quickly toggle the eye icon off and on); this usually restores the picture immediately.

steps.title: Lock the capture method to avoid "Automatic" drift
steps.detail: With Capture Method set to "Automatic", OBS may switch between WGC/BitBlt as the app state changes, and the moment the app switches render modes it tends to go black; explicitly locking one method reduces recurrence.

steps.title: Turn off hardware acceleration in the target app
steps.detail: In browsers, Electron apps, WPS/Office, and similar, turn off "Use hardware acceleration" in settings and restart the app to eliminate intermittent black screens caused by a separate swap chain.

steps.title: Change games to borderless windowed
steps.detail: Entering exclusive fullscreen makes Window Capture fail and go black instantly; change the game's display setting to "Borderless Window" to capture stably.

steps.title: Update the graphics driver and check overlay software
steps.detail: If sudden black screens come with GPU driver reset notices, update the graphics driver; also disable injecting overlays such as the Discord/Steam/GeForce overlay.

tips: Window Capture uses fewer resources and is safer than Display Capture
Sudden intermittent black screens are usually a failed capture handle: refresh the source to recover the stream, then work through the steps to fix the root cause
If the same app keeps going black, switching to Game Capture (hook mode) is usually more stable than Window Capture

problems.title: Windows 11 Display Capture black screen
symptoms: Display/Window Capture black screen on Win11
Capture stops working after a system update
causes: Win11 changed the hardware-accelerated capture mechanism
The default capture method is incompatible with the new system

steps.title: Turn off system hardware acceleration (if needed)
steps.detail: Settings → System → Display → Graphics → Change default graphics settings, turn off "Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling", then restart.

tips: On Win11, prefer the WGC capture method

problems.title: Black screen caused by laptop dual graphics (integrated + discrete)
symptoms: Game/desktop is black in OBS
Only happens on laptops; desktops are fine
causes: OBS runs on the integrated GPU while the game runs on the discrete GPU, and the two cannot communicate
Windows graphics settings assigned OBS to the power-saving GPU

steps.title: Assign OBS to the high-performance GPU in Windows graphics settings
steps.detail: Settings → System → Display → Graphics → Browse, add obs64.exe → Options → select "High performance" → Save and restart OBS.

steps.title: Set a consistent GPU in NVIDIA Control Panel
steps.detail: NVIDIA Control Panel → Manage 3D settings → Program Settings → add OBS → set Preferred graphics processor to "High-performance NVIDIA processor".

steps.title: Use Window Capture to sidestep GPU matching
steps.detail: Window Capture does not require matching GPUs and can serve as a temporary workaround.

tips: Dual graphics is the number one cause of black screens on laptops

problems.title: "Encoding overloaded" warning
symptoms: OBS status bar/log shows Encoding overloaded
Severe dropped frames and stutter while streaming or recording
causes: CPU encoding (x264) load is too high
Output resolution/frame rate set too high
Background programs consume resources
No hardware encoder is used

steps.title: Switch to a hardware encoder
steps.detail: Settings → Output → Encoder, select NVIDIA NVENC H.264 (NVIDIA), AMD AMF (AMD), or Intel QSV (integrated), to greatly reduce CPU load.

steps.title: Lower the output resolution
steps.detail: Settings → Video → Output (Scaled) Resolution, drop from 1920x1080 to 1280x720 for an immediate effect.

steps.title: Lower the frame rate
steps.detail: Settings → Video → Common FPS Values, drop from 60 to 30.

steps.title: Use a faster x264 preset / close background apps
steps.detail: If you stick with x264, change the preset to veryfast/superfast; close background programs such as browsers and other streaming software.

tips: Resolution x frame rate x bitrate form a triangle; lowering one makes the rest more stable
For game streaming, prefer NVENC

problems.title: High x264 CPU usage causes dropped frames
symptoms: Task Manager shows OBS CPU usage >90%
Frame rate collapses and the picture stutters
causes: Software encoding (x264) is used and the PC has too few cores
Running the game and encoding at the same time competes for resources

steps.title: Switch to hardware encoding
steps.detail: Change the encoder to NVENC/AMF/QSV to offload encoding from the CPU to the GPU.

steps.title: Reserve resources for OBS
steps.detail: Settings → Advanced → General → set Process Priority to "Above Normal"; for gaming laptops, use a separate machine or lower game quality.

steps.title: Limit the game frame rate
steps.detail: In the game, cap the frame rate at the monitor refresh rate to avoid needless CPU/GPU load.

tips: Pure CPU encoding only suits a dedicated recording PC or streaming without gaming

problems.title: Stutter caused by output resolution/frame rate set too high
symptoms: Stutters even on high-end hardware
Blurry stream or intermittent dropped frames
causes: Chasing 1080p60 blindly, beyond what the machine/network can handle
Canvas and output resolution do not match

steps.title: Match canvas and output resolution
steps.detail: Settings → Video → set Base (Canvas) Resolution and Output (Scaled) Resolution to match or scale reasonably to avoid stretching.

steps.title: Pick a tier that matches your machine
steps.detail: Use 720p30 on entry-level machines; 720p60 or 1080p30 on mid-range; go to 1080p60 only on high-end.

steps.title: Use a high-quality scaling filter
steps.detail: Set Output Scaling Filter to Lanczos (sharpened scaling) for better image quality.

tips: Stability matters more than high settings

problems.title: Streaming network dropped frames
symptoms: Stats dock Dropped Frames keeps growing above 0
Viewers see stutter and intermittent stream drops
causes: Insufficient upload bandwidth; bitrate exceeds a stable upload
Unstable route to the server
WiFi/VPN/security software interference

steps.title: Lower the video bitrate to 75% of your upload
steps.detail: Settings → Output → Video Bitrate, set it to about 75% of your stable upload speed (for a 10Mbps upload, set 6000-8000kbps).

steps.title: Use CBR with dynamic bitrate
steps.detail: Set Rate Control to CBR under Output; check "Dynamically change bitrate to manage congestion (Beta)" under Advanced → Network.

steps.title: Enable network optimizations / TCP pacing
steps.detail: Settings → Advanced → Network, check "Enable network optimizations" and "Enable TCP pacing" (Windows only).

steps.title: Change servers / use wired
steps.detail: Settings → Stream → switch to a lower-latency server; use wired networking when possible and avoid WiFi 2.4G.

tips: Upload x1.5 >= stream bitrate is the safe line
Streaming over WiFi is very prone to instability

problems.title: Rendering skipped frames
symptoms: Stats dock Skipped Frames > 0
Frames are skipped but the network is fine
causes: The capture device drops frames; insufficient VRAM
Scene is overloaded (too many filters/sources)
The render pipeline is blocked

steps.title: Simplify scenes and filters
steps.detail: Reduce unnecessary sources, filters, and transitions; close unused Scene Collections.

steps.title: Check VRAM and the capture device
steps.detail: Close programs that use VRAM; lower the resolution of the camera/capture card; make sure the device frame rate is stable.

steps.title: Reduce the rendering load
steps.detail: Lower the output resolution to 720p; turn off the preview (or shrink the preview window) to free rendering resources.

tips: Skipped points to rendering, Dropped points to network; tell them apart first

problems.title: Network send buffer stays high / stream drops
symptoms: Stats dock Network Send Buffer stays >80%
The stream disconnects mid-session
causes: Upload congestion
Router QoS wrongly throttles OBS
Aging network hardware

steps.title: Immediately lower the bitrate or switch networks
steps.detail: When the buffer stays high, lower the video bitrate right away or switch to 5GHz/wired networking.

steps.title: Turn off the router's QoS smart throttling
steps.detail: In the router, turn off features such as "smart bandwidth allocation" that may wrongly throttle OBS.

steps.title: Restart the modem/router
steps.detail: Restart the modem and then the router to rule out general connectivity issues.

tips: If any metric stays >5 for 30 straight seconds, it is unusable and you should downgrade

problems.title: Audio/video desync (sound and picture out of sync)
symptoms: Lip sync is off
Sound is ahead of or behind the picture
causes: Capture latency causes an offset
Manual sync offset compensation is needed

steps.title: Compensate with Sync Offset
steps.detail: Audio Mixer → gear icon for the source → Advanced Audio Properties → Sync Offset: enter a negative value (such as -200ms) when the sound is behind the picture, or a positive value when it is ahead, and fine-tune in 100ms steps.

steps.title: Check device latency
steps.detail: In Advanced Audio Properties, review each device's audio monitoring/latency value and use a common reference.

tips: First decide whether the sound is ahead or behind, then choose positive or negative

problems.title: Mismatched audio sample rate causes crackling/desync
symptoms: Crackling and noise
Recording/stream is out of sync
causes: System sound sample rate differs from OBS (44.1k vs 48k)
Multichannel (5.1/7.1) is not downmixed

steps.title: Set a uniform 48kHz sample rate
steps.detail: Windows Sound settings → playback/recording device Properties → Advanced → set Default Format to 48000 Hz; keep OBS audio settings the same.

steps.title: Enable resampling in OBS
steps.detail: If a device is not 44.1/48k, enable resampling to the target 48kHz in the OBS audio settings.

steps.title: Downmix multichannel to stereo
steps.detail: For 5.1/7.1 devices, add an "Audio Monitor" filter → enable "Downmix to Stereo" and set the output channel count to 2.

tips: 48kHz is the common standard for streaming

problems.title: Microphone has no sound / is not recognized
symptoms: Viewers cannot hear you talk
The microphone meter in the Audio Mixer does not move
OBS says there is no audio device
causes: Wrong device selected in OBS
The system does not recognize the microphone
The microphone is muted

steps.title: Select the correct microphone in OBS
steps.detail: Settings → Audio → Microphone/Auxiliary Audio Device, select the correct input; or add an "Audio Input Capture" source and specify the device.

steps.title: Confirm the system recognizes it
steps.detail: Windows Settings → System → Sound → Input devices, confirm the microphone exists and is not disabled; speak into the microphone and watch the level bar.

steps.title: Check the Audio Mixer meter and mute
steps.detail: In the OBS Audio Mixer, confirm the microphone meter moves when you speak; if it does not, the device is wrong or permissions are insufficient.

tips: Avoid letting system recording software and OBS grab the device at the same time

problems.title: Echo / feedback (double capture)
symptoms: Viewers hear an echo
Harsh feedback squeal
Your voice sounds repeated
causes: Desktop audio and microphone capture the same sound twice
Monitoring through speakers lets the microphone pick it back up
Windows Stereo Mix is enabled

steps.title: Monitor with headphones and disable speakers
steps.detail: Use headphones instead of speakers while streaming to keep the microphone from picking up the stream's sound and forming a loop.

steps.title: Turn off Stereo Mix
steps.detail: Windows Sound → Recording → disable Stereo Mix (when enabled, it feeds system sound back into the microphone).

steps.title: Check for duplicate capture sources
steps.detail: Confirm you have not added both "Desktop Audio" and several sources that pick up the same sound; keep only the necessary audio sources.

tips: Headphones are the simplest fix for echo

problems.title: Desktop audio / game sound is missing
symptoms: Viewers cannot hear game/desktop sound
The desktop audio meter does not move
causes: No desktop audio device is selected
The default playback device is not the current output
Channel/sample rate problem

steps.title: Select the desktop audio device in OBS
steps.detail: Settings → Audio → Desktop Audio Device, select the current default playback device (such as speakers/headphones).

steps.title: Add Audio Output Capture
steps.detail: Add an "Audio Output Capture" source and specify the correct output device.

steps.title: Check the system default device
steps.detail: In Windows Sound settings, confirm the default playback device matches the one in OBS.

tips: Desktop audio and microphone are two separate tracks; check them separately

problems.title: Stream connection timeout / failure
symptoms: Spins for a long time or errors out after you click Start Streaming
Says it cannot connect to the server
causes: Wrong stream address/key
Poor server choice
Unusual IP family/bind IP settings
Blocked by the firewall

steps.title: Verify the stream address and key
steps.detail: Settings → Stream → confirm the server address and Stream Key are exactly right (for custom RTMP, paste the server and key separately).

steps.title: Change servers and set IP family to IPv4
steps.detail: Settings → Stream → switch to a lower-latency/automatic server; Advanced → Network → set IP Family to "IPv4 only" and keep Bind to IP at "Default".

steps.title: Allow it through the firewall / temporarily disable security software
steps.detail: Add OBS to the firewall/antivirus exceptions; you can briefly disable security software to confirm whether it is blocking, then re-enable it and allow OBS.

tips: First use an official stream test tool (such as TwitchTest) on your machine to find the best server

problems.title: Stream drops mid-session
symptoms: The stream suddenly disconnects while live
Frequent reconnects
causes: Unstable upload/bitrate too high
Network hardware or ISP problem
VPN/network driver issue

steps.title: Enable dynamic bitrate and network optimizations
steps.detail: Advanced → Network, check "Dynamically change bitrate to manage congestion" and "Enable network optimizations".

steps.title: Update the network adapter driver
steps.detail: Download and install the latest driver from the motherboard/adapter vendor's website; old drivers often cause poor connections.

steps.title: Contact your ISP
steps.detail: If the stream still drops after the above, it may be a carrier routing issue; contact your ISP with details.

tips: Stream drops are almost always a network problem, rarely OBS itself

problems.title: VPN / security software / bundled NIC software interferes with the connection
symptoms: Streaming is unstable after connecting a VPN
Antivirus/optimizer software drops the stream
causes: VPN introduces unstable routing
Antivirus blocks OBS connections
Killer NIC / Lenovo Vantage and similar lower OBS priority

steps.title: Test with the VPN off
steps.detail: Temporarily turn off the VPN to confirm whether it is causing the instability.

steps.title: Whitelist OBS in your security software
steps.detail: Add OBS as an exception in your antivirus/firewall instead of leaving it off long-term.

steps.title: Handle bundled network software
steps.detail: In Lenovo Vantage, turn off Network Boost; for Killer NIC, uninstall the suite and install only the driver; for other "network optimizer" software, fully uninstall it and test.

tips: Many "optimizer" apps quietly throttle OBS

problems.title: Stream to Twitch
symptoms: First time connecting OBS to Twitch
Need to set bitrate/resolution
causes: Account not connected or Stream Key not entered
Video settings don't match the platform's recommendations

steps.title: Connect your Twitch account
steps.detail: Settings → Stream → Service: choose Twitch → Connect Account (or copy the Stream Key from the Creator Dashboard and paste it into "Use Stream Key").

steps.title: Set video encoding and bitrate
steps.detail: Output → Advanced → Encoder: NVENC / x264; 6000kbps CBR is recommended for 1080p60; 1280x720 is more stable.

steps.title: Choose a server
steps.detail: Server defaults to Auto; for stability, pick a nearby node such as "Asia: Tokyo".

tips: Twitch officially recommends 6000kbps CBR for 1080p60

symptoms: Connect OBS to Bilibili live
Get the stream URL
causes: Need to get the rtmp URL and Stream Key from the live room
Bitrate not set appropriately

steps.title: Recommended settings
steps.detail: For 1080p: video bitrate >6000kbps, audio 320kbps, resolution 1920x1080, frame rate 60 (if your machine can handle it).

tips: Bilibili recommends 6000kbps or higher for 1080p

problems.title: Douyin streaming (Live Companion) / Kuaishou OBS streaming
symptoms: Douyin can't stream via OBS
No OBS streaming entry found in Douyin's web go-live
Streaming to Kuaishou with OBS
causes: Douyin has officially stopped providing an OBS / third-party RTMP streaming entry; only the official "Douyin Live Companion" is supported
The web go-live OBS streaming entry has been taken down; the old stream code workflow no longer works

steps.title: Douyin: switch to the official "Douyin Live Companion"
steps.detail: Download and log in to Douyin Live Companion (the only official streaming tool), capture your screen directly with it, and go live — no longer through OBS streaming.

steps.title: Want to use the OBS picture in Live Companion
steps.detail: In OBS, enable "Virtual Camera" (Sources → Tools → Virtual Camera), then in Live Companion add a "Camera" source and select OBS Virtual Camera; or use the NDI plugin to forward the OBS picture to Live Companion.

steps.title: Kuaishou: follow the official live settings
steps.detail: Kuaishou mainly goes live with the official "Kuaishou Live Companion"; if the platform still provides an OBS streaming entry, copy the stream URL and stream code (Stream Key) from the live settings and enter them in OBS Settings → Stream → Custom.

steps.title: Don't capture the stream code from Live Companion for OBS
steps.detail: The community-circulated trick of "sniffing / reading the Live Companion stream code and entering it into OBS" is a gray-area practice, violates platform rules, risks a ban, and is not recommended.

tips: Douyin no longer provides an OBS streaming entry and officially supports only Live Companion; to use the OBS picture, rely on Virtual Camera / NDI forwarding
Before streaming to other platforms, click "Start Live" on the platform page first, then click "Start Streaming" in OBS — otherwise it often fails

problems.title: Custom RTMP streaming to Tencent Cloud
symptoms: Stream to Tencent Cloud Live (CSS) with OBS
Need to generate a stream URL
causes: Need an ICP-filed streaming domain
The stream URL contains authentication parameters

steps.title: Generate the stream URL
steps.detail: Tencent Cloud Live console → Common Tools → Address Generator → select stream URL, streaming domain, AppName (live), StreamName, expiration time → Generate.

steps.title: Enter in OBS
steps.detail: Settings → Stream → Custom: enter rtmp://domain/AppName/ in Server, and StreamName?txSecret=...&txTime=... in Stream Key.

steps.title: Reduce latency settings
steps.detail: Output → Advanced → Keyframe Interval (GOP): set to 2s; for ultra-low latency choose LEB (fast live) and turn off B-frames.

tips: LEB (fast live) does not support B-frames; disable B-frames on the streaming side

problems.title: Stream to multiple platforms at once (Restream)
symptoms: Stream to Bilibili + Douyin + Twitch, etc. at the same time
OBS natively streams only one destination
causes: OBS streams to only one target per session
Need a relay or plugin for multiple destinations

steps.title: Use an RTMP relay service
steps.detail: Sign up for a service such as Restream / cloud streaming relay, aggregate the multi-platform keys into a single RTMP target, and have OBS stream to just that one.

steps.title: Or use an OBS multi-output plugin
steps.detail: Install an output plugin such as multi-rtmp and add multiple streaming targets inside OBS (make sure your uplink and machine can handle it).

steps.title: Assess your upload bandwidth
steps.detail: Multi-destination streaming multiplies uplink usage; make sure upload ≥ total bitrate × 1.5, otherwise you'll get dropped frames.

tips: A relay service is the least hassle, but mind the latency and cost

problems.title: Recording file won't open / won't play
symptoms: Can't find the file after recording
Player says the format is unsupported/corrupt
causes: Recording format/encoder not supported by the player
Recording interrupted unexpectedly and not finalized
Wrong save path

steps.title: Use a widely compatible container format
steps.detail: Settings → Output → Recording: set Type to mp4 (or mkv, which is less prone to corruption); mkv can be converted with OBS's built-in "Remux Recordings" tool.

steps.title: Confirm the save path
steps.detail: Settings → Output → Recording → Recording Path: confirm the directory exists and is writable.

steps.title: Play with VLC
steps.detail: If your player doesn't support it, open it with VLC — it has the best compatibility.

tips: On an unexpected crash, prefer mkv to salvage more of the recording

problems.title: Recording shows a black screen
symptoms: The recorded file is black
Screen recording has no content
causes: The capture source itself is black
Wrong recording resolution/source settings

steps.title: Fix the capture source black screen first

problems.title: Record locally while streaming
symptoms: Want to keep a local recording while streaming
Don't know how to set it up
causes: Recording settings must be configured separately
Worried about affecting streaming performance

steps.title: Enable local recording
steps.detail: Set up Settings → Output → Recording → Recording Path; click "Start Recording" on the main window to run it alongside "Start Streaming".

steps.title: Separate recording and streaming encoding
steps.detail: Recording can use its own encoder/quality independent of streaming; if your machine can handle it, use hardware encoding for both.

steps.title: Weigh performance
steps.detail: Streaming + recording together adds load; if you get dropped frames, prioritize streaming or lower the recording resolution.

tips: Local recording during a stream is a solid backup

problems.title: HDR game/video capture looks washed out, too dark, or color-shifted
symptoms: Overall washed-out, too dark look after capturing HDR game footage
Recorded file has abnormal colors in a normal player
Preview doesn't match the final output
causes: OBS HDR mode is off, so an HDR source is treated as SDR
Color Format/Space/Range settings don't match
The preview is tone-mapped but the recording didn't apply the correct parameters

steps.title: Enable HDR in OBS
steps.detail: File → Settings → Advanced → Video: set Color Format to P010 (10-bit), Color Space to Rec.2100 (PQ), and Color Range to Limited.

steps.title: Set the capture card/source to the same format
steps.detail: In the Video Capture Device properties, also choose P010 / Rec.2100 (PQ) to match OBS.

steps.title: Use an HDR-capable encoder
steps.detail: Recording HDR requires HEVC (Main10) or AV1; H.264 isn't HDR-compatible. For HDR streaming, currently mainly YouTube supports it.

steps.title: Adjust the SDR preview brightness
steps.detail: The SDR white level in advanced settings (default 300 nits) controls the preview brightness and doesn't affect the recorded file itself.

tips: On a normal monitor that can't show HDR, a darker preview is normal
Viewing HDR footage requires an HDR-capable monitor and player

symptoms: Video Capture Device source shows no image, a black screen, or "No Signal"
The preview briefly flashes, then goes black
causes: Poor HDMI cable/port contact, or a cable that does not support the required spec

steps.title: Update the capture card driver/firmware

tips: A mismatched color range makes the image too dark or washed out; standardize on Limited/Partial first

symptoms: Periodic dropped frames and stutter when streaming over WiFi
Signal fluctuations cause intermittent stream dropouts
causes: 2.4 GHz WiFi is congested and its bandwidth is unstable
Too far from the router, or through walls
Devices on the same band compete for bandwidth

steps.title: Lower the bitrate for headroom

tips: Streaming demands very stable upload; treat WiFi as a temporary solution only

causes: Home broadband upload is inherently small

problems.title: Microphone/device sync offset (Sync Offset)
symptoms: Speech does not match lip movement; audio leads or lags
More noticeable after routing through a virtual camera / streaming app
causes: Each stage of the capture chain adds a different delay
A virtual camera / relay app (such as Live Companion) adds extra delay
Differences in device buffer settings

steps.title: Measure the delay with the clap method
steps.detail: Record yourself clapping, then in an editing app compare the timing of the clap sound against the frame where the hands meet; the difference is the number of milliseconds to compensate.

steps.title: Set the sync offset in Advanced Audio Properties
steps.detail: In the Audio Mixer, click the gear next to the microphone source → Advanced Audio Properties → Sync Offset (ms): enter a positive number if the audio is early (for example 150), or a negative number if it is late.

steps.title: Turn off microphone hardware buffering
steps.detail: Right-click the microphone source → Properties → uncheck "Use hardware buffering" to let OBS handle timing.

tips: Streaming directly with the Stream Key has less delay than routing through a virtual camera

problems.title: Audio/video desync that drifts over time (sample rate mismatch)
symptoms: In sync at first, then gradually and increasingly out of alignment after a few minutes
Progressive drift that keeps getting worse
causes: Windows sound, OBS, and the streaming app use different sample rates (44.1k vs 48k)
Accumulated device clock drift

steps.title: Set all sample rates to 48kHz
steps.detail: Set Windows sound settings, OBS (Settings → Audio → Sample Rate), and the streaming app all to 48kHz; never mix in 44.1k.

steps.title: Re-establish the sync offset baseline
steps.detail: After unifying the sample rate, re-measure with the clap method and enter the sync offset.

tips: A sample rate mismatch is the classic root cause of gradual drift

problems.title: Long recordings gradually drift out of sync (clock drift / disk saturation)
symptoms: Audio and video are in sync at first, but after an hour or two they drift clearly and keep diverging
Restarting OBS fixes it, but it slowly drifts again over time
Drift accelerates as the recording drive nears full
causes: The capture card, USB sound card, and Bluetooth headset each run on their own clock, with tiny deviations from the system clock that accumulate over time into second-level offsets
Variable frame rate (VFR) sources mixed with constant frame rate cause timestamps to gradually mismatch
When the recording disk is nearly full or write-saturated, audio frames cannot be written to disk in time to match their timestamps

steps.title: Unify the sample rate and switch to wired / direct-connected devices
steps.detail: Set all devices to 48kHz; prefer a wired microphone or a directly connected sound card, and avoid capturing voice over Bluetooth (the Bluetooth link has its own clock compensation).

steps.title: Apply Time Shift / sync offset correction to the drifting source
steps.detail: For a source confirmed to drift, add a millisecond-level timeline shift filter (such as the Time Shift plugin) or set a sync offset in Advanced Audio Properties to cancel the accumulated deviation.

steps.title: Keep headroom and write performance on the recording drive
steps.detail: Keep at least 10% free space on the recording drive; for long recordings, write to a local SSD rather than an external mechanical or network drive.

steps.title: Investigate VFR sources
steps.detail: Phone mirroring and some capture cards output a variable frame rate; fix the frame rate at the source where possible, or use post-processing that repairs VFR timestamps.

tips: "Drifts worse the longer it runs, fine after a restart" almost always points to clock drift rather than a settings error
Unify to 48kHz first, then measure the drift rate, to rule out most false drift

problems.title: Browser sources get laggier over a long stream (memory bloat)
symptoms: Smooth for the first few hours, then the overall frame rate slowly drops and the image stutters intermittently
In Task Manager, OBS memory usage keeps growing with stream length and never comes back down
Refreshing the browser source immediately relieves the stutter, but it worsens again later
causes: The web pages inside the browser source (chat overlay, counters, alert pages, etc.) leak memory, and the Chromium render process does not reclaim it
Page timers / animations pile up DOM and image resources over time
Multiple browser sources leak at once, and the memory overhead of AI-type plugins compounds the problem

steps.title: Refresh browser sources regularly
steps.detail: Right-click the browser source → Refresh (or set a reminder for the Interactive Window); refreshing rebuilds the render process and memory drops immediately. This is the most effective zero-cost measure.

steps.title: Trim the always-on page content
steps.detail: Remove unnecessary animations, carousels, and long chat histories; for a chat wall, keep only the most recent few entries scrolling.

steps.title: Reduce duplicate browser source instances
steps.detail: Do not create a separate copy of the same page in multiple scenes (each instance is a separate process); when reusing across scenes, share a single instance with Source Clone or nested scenes.

steps.title: Use local monitoring to find the culprit
steps.detail: Watch the memory curve on this app's Performance page: if memory rises linearly over time, refresh browser sources one by one and see when the curve drops to pinpoint the leak.

tips: "Gets laggier the longer you stream + fixed by refreshing" is the signature combination of a browser source leak
For long streams (over 6 hours), refresh all browser sources every 2~3 hours

problems.title: Plugin-Induced Crashes / Troubleshooting with Safe Mode
symptoms: Crashes or freezes on launch
Issues appear after adding a certain plugin
Crashes as soon as a specific feature is used
causes: The plugin is incompatible with the current OBS version
Plugin architecture mismatch (especially macOS Intel/Apple)
Plugin files are corrupted or conflicting

steps.title: First make sure OBS is updated to 32.2.2 or later
steps.detail: OBS 32.2 initially rewrote the Windows plugin DLL loading logic, so some plugins with dependencies failed to load on first launch; this was fixed in the 32.2.1 / 32.2.2 patch releases. Go to Settings → General → Check for Updates, or reinstall the latest version from the official site, then troubleshoot the plugin.

steps.title: Start in Safe Mode
steps.detail: Help → Launch OBS in Safe Mode loads only the core, to confirm whether it is a plugin issue.

steps.title: Update or remove the problem plugin
steps.detail: Download the version matching your current OBS from the plugin's official site; on macOS, be sure to pick the matching Apple/Intel architecture.

steps.title: Narrow it down one by one
steps.detail: Once Safe Mode works normally, re-enable plugins one by one to find the culprit.

tips: After a major OBS upgrade, old plugins often need updating to match

problems.title: Troubleshoot OBS Launch Crashes with Safe Mode (safe-mode)
symptoms: Double-clicking OBS closes it instantly or it does not respond
It crashes before reaching the main window
Only appears after installing a new plugin or a certain update
causes: Third-party plugin conflict
Corrupted graphics driver or runtime (Visual C++ Redistributable)
Corrupted config file

steps.title: Start in Safe Mode
steps.detail: Windows: hold Shift and double-click OBS, or append --safe-mode to the shortcut target; macOS: hold Alt while opening, or run open -n /Applications/OBS.app --args --safe-mode in Terminal. Safe Mode disables all plugins.

steps.title: Pinpoint the conflicting plugin
steps.detail: If Safe Mode opens normally, it is a plugin issue. Under Help → Plugins, disable recently installed plugins one by one, then start normally to verify.

steps.title: Repair the runtime/driver
steps.detail: On Windows, reinstall the latest Visual C++ Redistributable and update the graphics driver; if needed, delete %APPDATA%\obs-studio\crashes and try again.

steps.title: Roll back or reinstall OBS
steps.detail: If the config is corrupted, back it up and reinstall OBS; if the problem started with a certain update, download the previous stable version (e.g. 30.2.3).

tips: Safe Mode is the fastest way to tell a plugin issue from a problem with OBS itself
Before filing an issue, run the Log Analyzer first and attach the crash log

problems.title: Capturing Desktop/System Audio on macOS (BlackHole Virtual Device)
symptoms: On macOS there is no "Desktop Audio" device to capture
Only the microphone is recorded; game/video sound is lost
Want to stream the computer's own audio but the system provides no desktop audio source

The output device routing is wrong

steps.title: Install the BlackHole virtual audio driver
steps.detail: Install BlackHole 2ch (or 16ch) from github.com/ExistentialAudio/BlackHole, then restart OBS.

steps.title: Create a Multi-Output Device
steps.detail: Open "Audio MIDI Setup" → create a Multi-Output Device, check "Built-in Output" and "BlackHole 2ch", and set it as the system output, so you can both hear the sound and have OBS capture it.

steps.title: Add an Audio Input Capture in OBS
steps.detail: In OBS, Source → Audio Input Capture → select BlackHole 2ch as the device to mix system audio into your stream/recording.

tips: BlackHole is a free, open-source option that is lighter than paid virtual sound cards
A Multi-Output Device adds slightly higher latency; if you are latency-sensitive, use BlackHole alone

problems.title: NVENC Encoding Fails: Failed to open / Driver Initialization Error
symptoms: An NVENC error appears when starting the stream/recording
The log contains "Failed to open NVENC codec"
The encoder dropdown is empty or does nothing when selected
causes: The NVIDIA driver is too old or corrupted
The GPU is used by another program or the driver is blocked (e.g. by antivirus)
OBS is incompatible with the new driver version

steps.title: Update the NVIDIA graphics driver
steps.detail: Install the latest Game Ready driver from NVIDIA's site or via GeForce Experience, choosing "Clean Install" during setup.

steps.title: Check whether the encoder is in use
steps.detail: Close other software using NVENC (other streaming/screen-recording apps, CapCut, in-game recording) and use Task Manager to confirm no encoding processes are left over.

steps.title: Add antivirus/Defender exclusions
steps.detail: Add the OBS install directory to the Windows Defender exclusion list to keep the driver from being blocked; if needed, temporarily disable third-party antivirus to verify.

steps.title: Roll back or switch to another hardware encoder
steps.detail: If the new driver still fails, roll back to the previous stable driver; or switch to the AMD (AMF)/Intel (QSV) encoder, with x264 as a fallback.

tips: Prefer NVENC over x264 to free up the CPU
On laptops with dual GPUs, run OBS on the discrete GPU

problems.title: Black Screen When Capturing Anti-Cheat Games (Valorant / CS2 / Fortnite, etc.)
symptoms: Game Capture shows a black screen, but Display and Window Capture work
Games with anti-cheat such as Fortnite, Valorant and CS2 cannot be captured
The game can be captured in windowed mode but goes black in fullscreen
causes: The game's anti-cheat (Vanguard / VAC / Easy Anti-Cheat) blocks external programs from injecting capture hooks
The game runs in exclusive fullscreen, so the desktop composition layer is not visible
On dual-GPU laptops, OBS and the game use different GPUs

steps.title: Switch to Window Capture (WGC)
steps.detail: Set the game to "borderless windowed", add a Window Capture source, and choose the "Windows 10/11 (WGC)" capture method; this is the most reliable approach for games such as Valorant, Fortnite and Genshin.

steps.title: Force the game to run in DX11 mode
steps.detail: For Steam games, add -dx11 to the launch options; some games have a "Rendering API / Render Mode" setting, and switching from DX12 to DX11 often makes them capturable.

steps.title: Run OBS and the game on the same GPU
steps.detail: Laptop users: in Windows Settings → System → Display → Graphics, set both OBS and the game to "High performance (discrete GPU)" to avoid cross-GPU capture.

steps.title: Fall back to Display Capture
steps.detail: If it still cannot be captured, use Display Capture for the whole screen (requires administrator rights); be careful not to overlap the game window with private content.

tips: Do not put multiple Game Capture sources in one scene; use just one and set its target window
Close conflicting software such as the RTSS / MSI Afterburner / Discord overlay and try again

problems.title: Browser Source White Screen / Content Not Loading
symptoms: The Browser Source area is blank or white
Web content / the chat box / an animated wallpaper does not show
Sound works but the picture does not refresh
causes: The page itself forbids iframe embedding (X-Frame-Options / CSP)
The Browser Source needs network access or WebSocket permission
A GPU hardware-acceleration crash causes CEF rendering to fail
An error in custom CSS / JS leaves the page blank

steps.title: Confirm the page allows embedding
steps.detail: Some sites (e.g. a web dashboard behind a login) block iframe loading; switch to an embeddable URL, or use a "local HTML file + file:// protocol".

steps.title: Refresh / restart the Browser Source
steps.detail: Right-click the source → Refresh cache; if it is still blank, delete the source and add it again, which recovers most occasional CEF crashes.

steps.title: Disable hardware acceleration and retry
steps.detail: In the Browser Source properties, uncheck the acceleration options other than "still enable when hardware acceleration is off", or temporarily turn off hardware acceleration in Chrome to compare.

steps.title: Check local files and CSS
steps.detail: When a local HTML file uses the file:// protocol, its scripts / CSS cannot reference http resources (cross-origin requests are blocked); make sure there are no syntax errors.

tips: Browser Sources are resource-heavy and several of them will stutter, so merge them into one panel where possible
After a major OBS upgrade, Browser Sources occasionally go white; rebuilding the source usually fixes it

problems.title: Replay Buffer Won't Enable / Save Fails / Clips Lost
symptoms: "Enable Replay Buffer" is grayed out in Settings
Pressing the save hotkey does nothing or reports a failure
Saved clips are empty files / have a truncated beginning
causes: No recording / streaming encoder is configured; the Replay Buffer must rely on one of them
"Output Mode" is set to Advanced but no encoder is selected
Not enough disk space or a write-permission problem
The save hotkey is not set

steps.title: First enable the recording or streaming encoder
steps.detail: The Replay Buffer runs on the recording / streaming encoder. In Settings → Output, make sure an encoder (e.g. x264 / NVENC) is selected under the "Recording" or "Streaming" tab.

steps.title: Check the box and set the buffer duration
steps.detail: Settings → Output → Recording → check "Enable Replay Buffer" and set "Maximum Replay Time" to 30-120 seconds (longer uses more memory and disk).

steps.title: Set the save hotkey
steps.detail: Settings → Hotkeys → find "Save Replay Buffer" and bind a key combination (e.g. Ctrl+F8); press it during a stream to save the last segment.

steps.title: Check the disk and permissions
steps.detail: Make sure the disk holding the recording path has plenty of free space (at least several times the buffer duration) and that the directory is writable; switch to another drive if needed.

tips: Keep the buffer duration under 5 minutes, or memory usage will be high
After a long stream, when you press save, check the bottom-right corner for a save-success message before continuing

symptoms: OBS exits immediately or gets stuck on a black screen after launch

Appears after updating the graphics driver
causes: Graphics driver is incompatible with the OBS rendering interface (Direct3D 11)
Driver is corrupted or too old
Abnormal GPU switching on multi-GPU laptops

steps.title: Switch to the OpenGL renderer

steps.title: Update / roll back the graphics driver

steps.title: Force OBS to run on the dedicated GPU on laptops
steps.detail: Windows Settings → System → Display → Graphics → set OBS to 'High performance' (dedicated GPU); sometimes a failed iGPU initialization causes this error.

steps.title: Troubleshoot plugins in Safe Mode
steps.detail: Start with --safe-mode to rule out graphics-context initialization failures caused by third-party plugins.

tips: Keep the latest crash log (%AppData%\obs-studio\crashes) and upload it when you report the issue

problems.title: Green screen keying not clean / Chroma Key edge fringing
symptoms: Green halo or fringe around the subject's edges
See-through holes appear on clothing / skin
Noise shows through the background after keying
causes: Wrinkles, shadows, or uneven reflections on the green screen cloth
Insufficient lighting or green spill on the subject
Chroma Key parameters (Similarity / Smoothness / Spill Reduction) aren't tuned well
Poor webcam quality with heavy compression noise

steps.title: Light the green screen evenly
steps.detail: Light the green screen evenly with two lights to avoid wrinkles and shadows; keep the subject 1-2 m from the green screen to prevent green spill on them.

steps.title: Add a Chroma Key filter and adjust its parameters
steps.detail: Right-click the webcam → Filters → add Chroma Key: first raise Similarity to clean the key, then fine-tune Smoothness to remove edge fringing, and finally use Spill Reduction to remove green at the edges.

steps.title: Increase webcam clarity
steps.detail: In the webcam properties, set the resolution to 720p/1080p and turn off auto exposure and auto white balance; less compression noise means a cleaner key.

steps.title: Avoid green clothing
steps.detail: Don't wear green / neon clothing or green accessories, or they'll be keyed out along with the background.

tips: You don't need a 100% clean key; a little green at the edges looks better than noise across the whole frame
If you can, prefer a Virtual Background plugin or AI keying instead of relying on a green screen

problems.title: Media Source (local video / music) won't play, shows a green screen, or has no sound
symptoms: Green or black screen after adding a local video
Video plays but there's picture and no sound
Music file produces no audio after being added
Looping or stopping on end doesn't behave as expected
causes: Encoding format not supported by OBS (such as HEVC 10-bit, Dolby audio tracks, certain containers)
Audio track dropped by FFmpeg by default (multi-track mkv)
File reads slowly from an external / network drive
Loop and Stop on end options conflict

steps.title: Transcode before importing
steps.detail: Use HandBrake / Format Factory to convert the video to H.264 + AAC in an MP4 container for the best compatibility; OBS plays formats like HEVC 10-bit poorly.

steps.title: Enable 'Play audio track before media ends'
steps.detail: Media Source properties → Audio: for multi-track files you must select the track manually (Track 1/2/3); make sure 'Play audio track before media ends' is checked, or there will be no sound.

steps.title: Avoid playing directly from a network / USB drive
steps.detail: Copy the media to a local SSD before adding it; the read speed of USB 2.0 or a network drive causes stuttering and green screens.

steps.title: Check the loop and stop settings
steps.detail: If you want looping, check only Loop and not Stop on end; for music, use a Media Source + Loop.

tips: For background music while streaming, a Browser Source playing a playlist is better, since you can switch songs anytime
When recording, make sure the Media Source plays correctly in the preview before you start, to avoid surprises

problems.title: Text Source shows garbled Chinese / font not applied / won't display
symptoms: Chinese shows as boxes or garbled text in the Text Source
Selected Chinese font isn't applied; it always falls back to a default font
Text Source crashes or is blank right after being added
causes: Selected font doesn't support Chinese (such as Arial)
System font list loads incompletely / font cache is corrupted
Rendering differences between the old Text Source (text_ft2) and the new one (text_gdiplus)

steps.title: Choose a font that supports Chinese
steps.detail: In the Text Source properties, pick a Chinese font such as Microsoft YaHei / Source Han Sans / KaiTi, and use a font size of at least 24 to avoid a blurry, too-small render.

steps.title: Switch to the newer Text Source
steps.detail: OBS 30+ offers the new Text (GDI+) source, which renders Chinese better; the old Text (FreeType 2) has weaker Chinese support, so prefer the new one.

steps.title: Refresh the font cache
steps.detail: On Windows, delete the font cache files under %SystemRoot%\Fonts and restart (or rebuild the font cache service); on macOS, use Font Book to repair fonts.

steps.title: Use an image / Browser Source instead
steps.detail: For complex layouts (shadows, outlines, gradients), export a transparent PNG from a design tool or load HTML in a Browser Source for more controllable results.

tips: For animated text (marquees / chat overlays), a Browser Source with HTML/CSS is the easiest approach
Keep the stream title as its own text layer so you can change it anytime

problems.title: Scene transitions not working / switching looks abrupt
symptoms: Scene changes are hard cuts with no fade
A transition works only once after being selected
The Transition button is unavailable in Studio Mode
causes: No transition is selected in the transitions dock, or Cut is selected
Transition duration is set to 0ms
No transition set in Studio Mode (only the preview is configured)

steps.title: Select a transition in the transitions dock
steps.detail: In the Transition dropdown at the bottom of OBS, choose Fade / Cut / Slide, and so on; the number next to it is the duration (200-500ms recommended).

steps.title: Make sure the duration isn't 0
steps.detail: A transition duration of 0 is the same as a hard cut; set it back to around 300ms.

steps.title: Set both transitions in Studio Mode
steps.detail: In Studio Mode, the Preview Transition and Program Transition are set separately; only clicking the Transition button switches with a transition.

steps.title: Check plugins for custom transitions
steps.detail: If you use a Stinger / custom transition plugin, make sure the plugin file path and duration settings are correct.

tips: Keep transitions consistent while streaming; don't use a different fancy transition for every scene
Using Slide or a Stinger for going live / ending adds a nice sense of ceremony

problems.title: Microphone clipping / distortion (too much gain makes the audio crackle)
symptoms: Audio crackles or distorts when you talk loudly
The mic meter often hits the top and turns red in the Audio Mixer
Recorded files sound harsh with clipped waveforms
causes: Mic Gain or the system microphone boost is set too high
Too close to the mic or large swings in speaking volume
Device sample rate doesn't match OBS, causing noise

steps.title: Lower the gain until it stops clipping
steps.detail: In the Audio Mixer, set the mic volume to 60-80% and keep the meter out of the red zone even when you speak at your loudest; if needed, set the system 'Microphone Boost' to zero.

steps.title: Add a Limiter filter
steps.detail: Right-click the mic → Filters → add Limiter and set the threshold to around -6dB to catch sudden loud peaks.

steps.title: Noise suppression + compression for steadier audio
steps.detail: Add Noise Suppression (RNNoise) → Compressor (threshold -20dB, ratio 3:1) → Limiter in that order; your voice will be clearer and won't distort.

steps.title: Match the sample rate
steps.detail: Set the sample rate to 48kHz in both Windows sound settings and Settings → Audio in OBS to avoid noise.

tips: It's better to be too quiet than to clip - you can amplify later, but clipped detail is gone for good
Do a short test recording in OBS to check the waveform before going live

problems.title: High viewer-side latency (stream delayed by tens of seconds)
symptoms: Viewers see the picture more than 20 seconds behind real time
Chat interaction doesn't line up with the picture
The platform dashboard warns that latency is too high
causes: Large default buffering on the streaming platform (some default to 15-30 seconds)
High bitrate set by the streamer + platform transcoding queue
Network jitter makes the platform increase buffering

steps.title: Turn on low-latency mode
steps.detail: Most platforms (Bilibili / Twitch, etc.) or the Douyin streaming companion have a 'Low Latency' option that can cut it to 5-8 seconds; no change is needed on the OBS side.

steps.title: Use the correct streaming protocol
steps.detail: When the platform supports it, prefer RTMPS or SRT (newer platforms); they have lower latency and better packet-loss resilience than classic RTMP.

steps.title: Moderately lower the bitrate
steps.detail: If your upload is unstable, using more than 6000kbps at 1080p60 makes the platform increase buffering; dropping to 4500-5000kbps is more stable.

steps.title: Check platform transcoding
steps.detail: Check the streaming dashboard for a transcoding status; on some platforms, forced transcoding for less popular streams adds latency, so you can contact support to adjust it.

tips: For interactive streams (chat, Q&A), always enable low latency; for on-demand content (course replays), a bit more latency is fine
Higher latency on a poor network is the platform protecting itself - don't try to force both low-latency mode and a high bitrate

problems.title: Random audio/video desync during a stream (off by seconds after a few hours)
symptoms: After more than an hour of streaming, viewers report audio/video off by a few seconds
Audio speeds up and slows down, drifting repeatedly
Log says Audio buffering hit the maximum value
causes: High system load fills the OBS audio buffer
Incorrect timestamps from certain audio devices
Game / system volume changes trigger a buffer reset
Unstable latency on wireless / Bluetooth devices

steps.title: Turn on Windows Game Mode
steps.detail: Settings → Gaming → Game Mode → turn it on. Game Mode gives OBS more stable scheduling and reduces audio buffer swings.

steps.title: Restart OBS to reset the buffer
steps.detail: After random desync appears, restart OBS first (just restarting the stream won't help). OBS has confirmed that device timestamp errors make the buffer keep growing, and a restart resets it.

steps.title: Reduce system load
steps.detail: Close unnecessary programs (browser tabs, cloud sync) and watch CPU usage; under heavy load the audio buffer easily hits its limit.

steps.title: Avoid wireless audio devices
steps.detail: Bluetooth headphones / wireless mics have unstable latency; prefer wired devices for monitoring and capture while streaming.

tips: Before a long stream, record 30 minutes of test footage to check audio/video sync
If the log (Help → Log Files) shows an audio buffering message, it's almost always a load or timestamp issue

problems.title: Microphone processing chain: noise suppression → gate → compression → limiting
symptoms: Vocals mixed with fan / keyboard / electrical hum
Speaking volume keeps jumping up and down
Crackling when excited and inaudible when quiet
causes: Only noise suppression was added, with no dynamics processing
Wrong filter order; noise suppression last brings the noise back
Gain too high, causing clipping

steps.title: Add the filters in the correct order
steps.detail: Right-click the mic → Filters → add in order: Noise Suppression (RNNoise) → Noise Gate → Compressor → Limiter. The wrong order makes it worse.

steps.title: Choose RNNoise for noise suppression
steps.detail: For Noise Suppression, choose the RNNoise method (clearly better than the old Speex); a level of 10-15 is enough, and higher settings swallow words.

steps.title: Compressor parameter reference
steps.detail: Compressor: threshold -18 to -24dB, ratio 3:1 to 4:1, attack 5ms, release 100ms. This makes quiet parts clearer and loud parts clean.

steps.title: Limiter as a safety net
steps.detail: Limiter: threshold -6dB. It catches sudden spikes like a burst of laughter or a slap on the desk so nothing clips.

tips: After tuning the filter chain, record a short test in OBS and check that the mixer waveform is steady
Use Monitor and Output for monitoring, then fine-tune based on what you hear in real time

problems.title: Stream Key leaked / someone else streaming as you / key security
symptoms: Someone else goes live on your account
Content you didn't stream shows up on your channel
The Stream Key is visible in a screenshot / screen recording
causes: The Stream Key is like a channel password and leaks through screenshots / sharing
Pasting the key into a public chat / forum while asking for help
Several people sharing the same key configuration

steps.title: Reset the key immediately
steps.detail: Twitch: Creator Dashboard → Settings → Stream → Primary Stream Key → Reset; on Bilibili / Douyin / YouTube, reset it under the stream settings in the live dashboard. The old key stops working at once.

steps.title: Prefer Connect Account over a manual key
steps.detail: OBS 28+ supports Settings → Stream → choose Twitch / YouTube as the Service → Connect Account; after you authorize, there's no key to copy and paste, so it's leak-resistant by design.

steps.title: Censor before sharing a screenshot
steps.detail: Before screenshotting the stream settings page, click Hide Key or blur it; when asking for help, don't post a full screenshot that includes the key / stream URL.

steps.title: Sync all devices after a new key
steps.detail: After resetting, update every computer / phone / hardware encoder using that key, or the old devices will drop the stream.

tips: The key is a publishing credential, not your account password, but a leak is as bad as losing your account
Always reset it when you change streamers / after an employee leaves

problems.title: OBS shows connected, but the platform has no picture / shows offline
symptoms: OBS status bar shows streaming and the bitrate fluctuates
The platform dashboard shows offline or that the stream isn't live
Viewers see a black screen / no content when they open the channel
causes: Key expired or mistyped (changed but not updated)
Wrong streaming server / region selected
Stream URL is missing a path or is a web page address
Firewall blocks some outbound connections

steps.title: Re-copy and paste the key
steps.detail: Copy the latest key from the platform dashboard and paste it into Settings → Stream in OBS, taking care not to include leading or trailing spaces. You must re-copy it after a key reset / a 2FA change.

steps.title: Check the service and server
steps.detail: Always choose the platform's built-in Service option (Twitch / custom RTMP for Bilibili), select Auto or the nearest server, and don't type a web page address.

steps.title: Verify with bandwidth test mode
steps.detail: On Twitch, append ?bandwidthtest=true to the server URL; on platforms like Bilibili, do a private / unpublished stream as a test. Confirm that OBS-side encoding is normal.

steps.title: Check the firewall / antivirus
steps.detail: Make sure the firewall allows outbound connections from OBS (obs64.exe); corporate / campus networks may block RTMP ports such as 1935.

tips: For connected but no picture, check the key and server first; don't blame your PC's performance right away
Resetting the key mid-stream drops the stream at once and OBS shows no error

problems.title: Virtual Camera won't work / doesn't appear / shows a black screen
symptoms: OBS Virtual Camera is missing in the meeting app
It appears but the picture is black / frozen
The preview is fine, but the other side can't see the picture
causes: The meeting app was opened first and the Virtual Camera started later, so the device list wasn't refreshed
Wrong Virtual Camera output target (for example, outputting an empty preview)
Camera access for desktop apps is turned off in Windows

steps.title: Set the output target to Program

steps.title: Turn on Windows camera access
steps.detail: Settings → Privacy & security → Camera → turn on 'Camera access' and 'Let desktop apps access your camera'.

steps.title: Rule out conflicts and reinstall
steps.detail: Close other virtual camera apps such as Snap Camera / ManyCam; if the problem persists, reinstall OBS (the Virtual Camera component is registered by the installer).

problems.title: Multiple capture sources in one scene interfere with each other (black screen / flicker)
symptoms: The picture flickers when a scene has both Display Capture and Game Capture
Two Game Capture sources fight over the game
The capture goes bright and dark, with high resource usage
causes: Multiple capture sources hook the same GPU composite layer at once and interfere
Mixing Display / Game / Window Capture in one scene
A separate capture source per game causes frequent switching

steps.title: Keep only one kind of capture source per scene
steps.detail: Don't put Display Capture, Game Capture, and Window Capture in the same scene; for multiple pictures, use different scenes combined with a Scene Source.

steps.title: Share one Game Capture across all games
steps.detail: In a single Game Capture source, check 'Capture any fullscreen application' and use hotkey mode (press a hotkey to pick the current game) to avoid creating several sources that fight each other.

steps.title: Use Window Capture instead of Game Capture
steps.detail: If a game you play often captures as a black screen, switch to Window Capture + Windows 10/11 (WGC), again keeping just one.

steps.title: Run OBS and the game on the same GPU
steps.detail: On a laptop, set both OBS and the game to 'High performance' (dedicated GPU) in Windows graphics settings to reduce cross-GPU interference.

tips: Fewer sources means more stability: don't use two capture sources when one will do
While streaming, keep the current scene clean first; preview scenes can be complex

problems.title: Webcam picture is blurry / stutters / low frame rate
symptoms: Webcam picture is soft and unclear
Video Capture Device drops frames and stutters

causes: Webcam resolution / frame rate set above what the device supports

Driver not updated or incompatible with the system

steps.title: Turn on camera access

steps.title: Update / reinstall the driver
steps.detail: Install the latest driver from the webcam maker's website; in OBS you can add a Sharpen filter (around 0.3) to slightly improve clarity.

tips: A lot of blurriness is just poor focus: focus first with the camera's own software
For filming people, 1080p30 + good front lighting is more practical than 4K at a high frame rate

problems.title: Corrupted config / restore defaults after messing it up (back up before resetting)
symptoms: OBS settings don't take effect no matter what you change
The UI misbehaves / errors appear frequently after some glitch
You want a clean slate but don't want to lose your scene setup
causes: Config file corrupted or a plugin wrote bad data
Parameters contradict each other after repeated tinkering
You want to troubleshoot but don't know where to start

steps.title: Back up the config first
steps.detail: After closing OBS, copy the entire %AppData%\obs-studio folder to your desktop as a backup (macOS: ~/.config/obs-studio). Your scenes / sources / settings are all in there.

steps.title: Rebuild a baseline with the Auto-Configuration Wizard
steps.detail: Tools → Auto-Configuration Wizard, run it again based on your network and use case to generate a solid bitrate / resolution baseline.

steps.title: Create a new profile instead of deleting the old one
steps.detail: Settings → Profile → New, keeping the old profile so you can roll back; the same goes for scene collections.

steps.title: Full reset
steps.detail: If you really need to wipe it, exit OBS and rename %AppData%\obs-studio\global.ini (or delete the profiles / scenes subfolders); restarting OBS rebuilds the default config.

tips: Back up first → change step by step → change only one variable at a time is the general method for troubleshooting any config problem
Reinstalling OBS doesn't delete %AppData%\obs-studio, so delete it manually for a clean slate

problems.title: Dropped frames caused by Windows Game Mode / performance mode being off
symptoms: The game runs smoothly but OBS drops rendered frames
The stream bitrate is fine but the picture stutters
Task Manager shows low OBS usage but the frame rate is unstable
causes: Windows Game Mode is off, so the scheduler doesn't reserve GPU time slices for OBS
Power mode is set to Power saver, throttling the CPU/GPU
Background programs compete for resources

steps.title: Turn on Game Mode
steps.detail: Settings → Gaming → Game Mode → turn it on; Game Mode makes Windows prioritize resources for the foreground game + OBS.

steps.title: Set the power mode to Best performance
steps.detail: Settings → System → Power → change the power mode to 'Best performance' (more stable when streaming on a laptop plugged in).

steps.title: OBS process priority
steps.detail: Task Manager → Details → OBS_Helper / obs64.exe → set the priority to 'Above normal' (you'll need to set it again after restarting OBS).

steps.title: Close high-usage background programs
steps.detail: While streaming, quit CPU/GPU-heavy programs such as cloud sync, extra browser tabs, and video rendering.

tips: When streaming with two monitors, putting OBS on its own screen and using Fullscreen Projector further reduces dropped frames
Check GPU usage first for dropped rendered frames; only check bandwidth for dropped network frames

problems.title: Wrong Keyframe Interval setting causes artifacts / blur
symptoms: Viewers often see blocky / corrupted picture
It takes a long time to become clear again after switching
The platform's transcoding quality options aren't available
causes: Keyframe Interval left on Auto, which doesn't meet the platform's 2-second requirement
The platform transcoder needs fixed keyframes to offer multiple qualities
Low bitrate + too long a keyframe interval makes the picture blurry

steps.title: Set it to a fixed 2 seconds
steps.detail: Settings → Output → Advanced Output → Streaming → set Keyframe Interval to 2 (seconds). Twitch / YouTube / Bilibili generally require 2 seconds, and the platform's transcoding quality options depend on it.

steps.title: Check the encoder's advanced parameters
steps.detail: With x264, keyint=2 is controlled by the setting; for NVENC, enter 2 in Advanced Output as well. Don't override it with command-line parameters at the same time.

steps.title: Don't push resolution when the bitrate is too low
steps.detail: 1080p60 needs at least 6000kbps; if your upload can't keep up, lower the output resolution (1600x900 / 720p), which looks far better than high resolution + artifacts.

tips: Artifacts are a sign of lost keyframes: check keyint first, then check network packet loss
Recommended platform bitrate table: 1080p60 = 6000kbps, 720p60 = 4500kbps

problems.title: Enable Dynamic Bitrate when your network fluctuates
symptoms: Occasional network jitter causes frequent dropped frames
The picture stutters repeatedly when WiFi / upload is unstable
You don't want to lower your fixed bitrate but still want stability
causes: A fixed bitrate can't adjust automatically when the network fluctuates
The platform drops packets outright for bursts above the top bitrate
The wireless network itself is jittery

steps.title: Enable Dynamic Bitrate
steps.detail: Settings → Advanced → Network → check Enable Dynamic Bitrate. When the network degrades, OBS lowers the bitrate automatically to stay smooth and raises it again once it recovers.

steps.title: Set a baseline with a bandwidth test
steps.detail: Run a bandwidth test first to confirm your usable upload, then set the ideal bitrate to about 80% of the available bandwidth, leaving headroom for fluctuation.

steps.title: Use wired if you can
steps.detail: Dynamic Bitrate is a patch; a wired network plus a stable router is the real fix. For long-term streaming, a cable is strongly recommended.

tips: With Dynamic Bitrate on, dropped frames during a stream drop noticeably, but bitrate swings may make the picture fluctuate slightly, which is normal
Pair it with the Auto Reconnect setting (Advanced → Network) so the stream recovers automatically after a drop

problems.title: Uncapped frame rate in-game maxes out the GPU, causing OBS rendering lag
symptoms: The game runs smooth at 200+ fps, but OBS rendering skips frames
Rendering Lag keeps climbing in the OBS Stats
GPU usage is at 100%, so OBS gets no resources
causes: The game has no VSync / no frame rate cap, so it saturates the GPU
On a single-GPU setup, OBS has to share the GPU with the game
Rendering lag and network dropped frames get mistaken for the same problem

steps.title: Cap the frame rate in-game
steps.detail: Turn on VSync in the game settings or set the frame rate cap to 60 / 120, leaving GPU time slices for OBS compositing and encoding.

steps.title: Lower demanding graphics settings
steps.detail: Dial down the heavy hitters like volumetric fog, shadows, and anti-aliasing. OBS needs roughly 5-10% of GPU headroom.

steps.title: Turn off the OBS preview to cut load
steps.detail: Lower the preview resolution or right-click the preview → Disable Preview to free up some GPU rendering load.

steps.title: Combine hardware encoding with a lower resolution
steps.detail: Use NVENC / AMF hardware encoding and scale the output down to 720p so encoding stops competing for the game's general-purpose GPU units.

tips: In the Stats dock, a rising Rendering Lag means the GPU is short on resources, not a network problem
A dual-PC setup (gaming PC + capture PC) fixes single-GPU resource contention at the root

problems.title: Read the Stats dock: dropped frames / rendering lag / encoder overload
symptoms: You can't tell whether stream stuttering is a network or a PC problem
The wall of numbers in the Stats dock makes no sense
All the different dropped frames talk is confusing
causes: Different metrics point to different bottlenecks: dropped frames = network, rendering/encoding lag = performance

steps.title: Open the Stats dock
steps.detail: View → Stats. Watch the three kinds of metrics live while streaming / recording.

steps.title: Dropped Frames rising → network problem
steps.detail: Steadily rising dropped frames mean your upload bandwidth is short or the network is jittery: lower the bitrate, switch to wired, and enable Dynamic Bitrate.

steps.title: Rendering Lag rising → GPU problem
steps.detail: Rising rendering lag means OBS is compositing frames too slowly: cap the in-game frame rate, lower graphics settings, and turn off the preview.

steps.title: Encoder Overloaded → CPU/encoder problem
steps.detail: If you see an encoder overload warning: switch to hardware encoding (NVENC/AMF), lower the resolution and frame rate, and pick a faster x264 preset.

tips: Healthy readings: 0-1% dropped frames, bitrate close to the set value, and low CPU usage
When it stutters, check the Stats first, then change settings, so you don't tweak blindly

problems.title: Recording files too large / not enough disk space
symptoms: 1 hour of video takes up tens of GB
A low disk space warning appears mid-recording
The recording folder is on the system drive, filling up C:
causes: Bitrate / quality set too high (high-bitrate CBR or too low a CRF)
The recording path defaults to the system drive
At the same resolution, a higher frame rate means a bigger file

steps.title: Move the recording path to a bigger drive
steps.detail: Settings → Output → Recording → change the Recording Path to a drive with plenty of free space (avoid C:).

steps.title: Use CRF / quality mode instead of CBR
steps.detail: For recording, use Advanced Output → Recording → Rate Control = CRF (about 18-20 for x264; CQ 20-22 for NVENC), which is far smaller than CBR at the same quality.

steps.title: Lower resolution / frame rate as needed
steps.detail: 1080p30 is usually enough for local footage; you don't need 4K60 for everything. Switch to a higher spec only when you're editing a replay.

steps.title: Transcode and archive promptly
steps.detail: After recording, transcode to H.265 with HandBrake and archive, which can halve the size again; or regularly clean up raw footage you don't need.

tips: 1 hour of 1080p60 @ 20000kbps ≈ 9GB; estimate your disk needs from that
When streaming + recording at the same time, recording can use CRF on its own to keep quality, independent of the streaming bitrate

problems.title: StreamFX discontinued: broken features / crashes (migration guide to alternatives)
symptoms: OBS crashes on startup or the plugin fails to load after installing StreamFX
After a major OBS upgrade, all StreamFX filters vanish or throw errors
The log shows os_dlopen(streamfx) failed / module load failed
causes: The StreamFX project is effectively discontinued and no longer keeps up with the OBS 30+ API
Old tutorials still recommend installing it, so you hit compatibility problems with the new OBS right after
For each of its individual features, actively maintained lightweight plugins have long been drop-in replacements

steps.title: Uninstall StreamFX first, then investigate
steps.detail: Start in Safe Mode (--safe-mode) to confirm it's causing the crashes, then just uninstall StreamFX. Don't keep retrying on a discontinued version.

steps.title: Blur → Composite Blur
steps.detail: High-quality Dual Kawase blur with good performance and results, the community successor to the StreamFX blur.

steps.title: Mask / shape crop → Advanced Masks
steps.detail: Full coverage for shape, gradient, and image masks, good for rounded webcam frames and custom-shaped video.

steps.title: Stroke, glow, shadow → Stroke Glow Shadow
steps.detail: A three-in-one filter that gives your webcam image a polished look in one step.

steps.title: Custom shaders → obs-shaderfilter
steps.detail: If you want the StreamFX shader workflow, use exeldro's shaderfilter to load community shaders.

tips: Back up your Scene Collection before migrating: Tools → Scene Collection Manager, export a copy so you don't lose filter parameters
On the Plugins page, use the local health check to confirm StreamFX is fully removed, then install the replacement plugins one by one

problems.title: obs-multi-rtmp multi-platform streaming is unstable (bandwidth drops / encoder overload / antivirus false positives) and alternatives
symptoms: When streaming to several platforms at once, total bandwidth drops suddenly and one stream keeps dropping frames
After enabling multi-streaming, the encoder overloads and the stream stutters
The installer or DLL is quarantined by antivirus as a false positive
causes: obs-multi-rtmp has become less reliable on newer OBS (the community reports sudden bandwidth drops and encoder overload)
Concurrent streams need upload bandwidth equal to the sum of every stream's bitrate; if the budget is short, they inevitably squeeze each other
DLLs distributed through unofficial channels easily trip antivirus heuristics

steps.title: Evaluate Aitum Multistream first
steps.detail: Actively maintained, with an independent bitrate and settings per stream, currently the mainstream recommendation for multi-platform streaming; you can migrate old configs directly.

steps.title: Check your bandwidth budget
steps.detail: Keep the sum of all stream bitrates under 70% of your measured upload bandwidth; if it's not enough, lower the bitrate / resolution per stream or cut the number of concurrent platforms.

steps.title: Handling antivirus false positives
steps.detail: Download the installer from the official GitHub Releases, verify it, then whitelist it. Don't download from unknown mirror sites.

steps.title: Verify each stream before going live
steps.detail: Test each stream first with a private / unlisted broadcast to check video and audio, watch the Stats dock for dropped frames, and only then go public.

tips: Use the platform's Account Connect or standard RTMPS for the main stream and route the extra ones through the plugin, so problems are easier to pinpoint
Dynamic Bitrate only affects the main output; stability on the extra streams depends entirely on reserved bandwidth headroom

problems.title: Third-party plugins fail to load / Safe Mode keeps popping up after updating OBS
symptoms: After upgrading OBS, startup shows an unverified plugin warning or goes straight into Safe Mode
The log shows Failed to load module / incompatible
A plugin's dock / filter disappears from the menus
causes: OBS 32.2 rewrote the Windows plugin DLL loading logic, so a few plugins with dependencies failed to load on first start (fixed in 32.2.1 / 32.2.2)
The plugin version is too old and incompatible with the new OBS API
After macOS forced the migration to Apple Silicon, Intel plugin builds no longer load
Leftover files from an old plugin version conflict with the new version of the same name

steps.title: First update OBS to the latest patch release
steps.detail: The plugin loading issue introduced in 32.2 is fixed in 32.2.2; Settings → General → Check for Updates, or reinstall the latest version from the website.

steps.title: Reinstall the plugin's current Release
steps.detail: Download the latest installer for your OBS version from the plugin's GitHub Releases and reinstall; this solves it in most cases.

steps.title: Still broken: delete clean, then install
steps.detail: Delete the old DLLs under <OBS folder>\obs-plugins\64bit\ and the matching folder under data\obs-plugins\, then reinstall, to avoid mixing old and new files.

steps.title: macOS users: switch to a universal binary
steps.detail: Apple Silicon machines must use an installer labeled universal / arm64; Intel plugin builds will no longer load.

tips: Before a major update, note down your installed plugin list so it's easy to compare if something breaks
The DLL name right after Failed to load module in the log is the culprit
