problems.title: Nahimic / RivaTuner (RTSS) / Overwolf and similar components interfere with OBS
symptoms: OBS crashes often, but the log shows no OBS error itself
Game Capture is a black screen / shows only a black frame
The frame rate is abnormally low or the recording file is corrupted
causes: The Nahimic audio service injects a DLL into the process and is a frequent cause of OBS crashes (preinstalled on MSI / Lenovo and other motherboards)
The RivaTuner / RTSS in-game overlay conflicts with the capture hooks
Overwolf, Voicemod, and the like also inject into or hook graphics and audio

steps.title: Uninstall or disable Nahimic
steps.detail: Uninstall Nahimic / A-Volute from the app list; on prebuilt PCs you can disable the Nahimic service. This is the number-one interference source repeatedly confirmed on the official forums.

steps.title: Turn off the RTSS overlay or whitelist OBS
steps.detail: In the RTSS settings, turn off On-Screen Display or turn off detection for obs64.exe, keeping only background monitoring.

steps.title: Investigate other injection-style software
steps.detail: Quit Overwolf / Voicemod / each game-boost utility (like the NVIDIA App overlay) one at a time to check; narrow it down by elimination.

steps.title: Run OBS as administrator
steps.detail: Right-click the shortcut → Run as administrator to reduce UAC and injection conflicts; also turn off anything like Enable in-game overlay.

tips: If the timestamps of the crash dumps (%AppData%\obs-studio\crashes) line up with those apps' service logs, that confirms it
Before reinstalling system-level audio software, try disabling its service first, which is enough in many cases

problems.title: Mismatched multi-monitor refresh rates cause stuttering / micro dropped frames
symptoms: With two monitors, the stream / recording stutters periodically
Render time in the Stats dock spikes intermittently
Everything is fine on one screen, but dropped frames start as soon as you add a second
causes: The two monitors have different refresh rates (like 144Hz + 60Hz), and the DWM compositor's cross-screen sync drags down rendering
A Browser / Window Capture lands on a screen with a different refresh rate

steps.title: Put OBS on the screen with the same refresh rate as the captured content
steps.detail: Keep the preview window and the captured game on the main screen (usually the one with the higher refresh rate) as much as possible; avoid a Window Capture source spanning screens.

steps.title: On Windows 11, turn on Optimizations for windowed games or switch to WGC capture
steps.detail: In the Window Capture properties, switch to Windows Graphics Capture (WGC) to bypass the old BitBlt cross-refresh-rate issue.

steps.title: Discrete GPU direct output / adjust GPU allocation
steps.detail: On laptops, point both OBS and the game to the discrete GPU in the graphics control panel; on desktops, make sure the monitor is plugged into the discrete GPU port.

tips: In View → Stats, a render time consistently above 10ms means a rendering-side problem, not the network
A 60Hz secondary screen showing only static info pages (chat, comments) has the least impact

problems.title: Steam version of OBS: plugins won't install / can't find the plugin folder
symptoms: You look for C:\Program Files\obs-studio as online tutorials say, but the folder isn't there
You copy the plugin DLL over, but nothing happens in OBS
All plugins vanish after a Steam update
causes: The Steam version installs into the Steam library folder (possibly not on C:), not the default Program Files path
The plugin was copied to the wrong sub-level (it must be bin\64bit)
Steam's file integrity check wipes added files that aren't on its whitelist

steps.title: Find the real install folder
steps.detail: Steam Library → right-click OBS Studio → Manage → Browse local files. A typical path looks like …\steamapps\common\OBS Studio.

steps.title: Place plugins in the standard structure
steps.detail: Put the DLL in <that folder>\obs-plugins\64bit\ and the plugin's data folder in <that folder>\data\obs-plugins\; the levels must be right.

steps.title: Prefer the plugin's own installer
steps.detail: Most popular plugins ship a Setup installer that auto-detects OBS folders, including Steam, and is more reliable than copying by hand.

steps.title: Less hassle: the user-level plugin folder
steps.detail: OBS 30.2+ supports admin-free installs: a %APPDATA%\obs-studio\plugins\<plugin name>\bin\64bits\x64.dll structure that Steam's integrity check won't wipe.

tips: After restarting OBS, check the log file to see whether the module is listed as loaded successfully
Don't mix the Steam version with the standalone installer; they share the same data folder and easily clash

problems.title: OBS starts slowly / hangs on the splash screen for a long time
symptoms: It takes tens of seconds after double-clicking the icon before the main window appears
The splash screen gets stuck at the loading Scene Collection stage
Every startup feels slower than the last
causes: You have many plugins, and a few initialize slowly or even time out online (like an update-checking plugin)

steps.title: Find the slow plugin by halving
steps.detail: Move half the DLLs out of obs-plugins\64bit and restart, narrowing it down step by step; once found, report it on the project page or switch to an alternative.

steps.title: Trim the Scene Collection and Browser Sources
steps.detail: Delete Scenes / Sources you never use; set Browser Sources to Shutdown source when not visible to cut the batch of web page loads at startup.

steps.title: Whitelist OBS in your antivirus
steps.detail: Add obs64.exe and the plugin folder to Defender / third-party antivirus exclusions so it isn't fully scanned on every startup.

tips: Help → Log Files → View Current Log; each module load line has a timing, so the slowest one stands out at a glance
Regularly clean the %AppData%\obs-studio\crashes and logs folders

problems.title: Device removed / GPU hang reset reported while streaming
symptoms: The log shows device removed / GPU hung / D3D device lost
The stream freezes for an instant or shows artifacts, then recovers
Accompanied by a system prompt about a graphics driver timeout
causes: The GPU stays maxed out for a long time (game + encoding stacked), triggering a driver TDR timeout reset
VRAM runs out (high resolution / multiple filters / a texture-heavy game stacked)
A graphics driver bug or an unstable core (overclocking / too-high VRAM overclock)
Insufficient power or poor cooling causes a momentary GPU fault

steps.title: Restore default clocks
steps.detail: Zero out all overclocks from tools like MSI Afterburner (especially the VRAM overclock); unstable VRAM is the most common trigger for device removed.

steps.title: Lighten the GPU load
steps.detail: Cap the in-game frame rate (for example 141/58) and lower graphics presets to leave headroom for OBS encoding; NVENC uses a dedicated hardware unit, so prefer hardware encoding.

steps.title: Clean-reinstall the graphics driver

problems.title: Picture turns into a mosaic / heavy blockiness (insufficient or fluctuating bitrate)

problems.title: Bluetooth headset as a microphone: muffled voice, high latency, audio/video drift
symptoms: After connecting a Bluetooth headset, the recording quality drops noticeably and sounds like a phone call
The sound comes half a second after your lips move, and audio gradually desyncs from video
It's worse when you both listen through the Bluetooth headset and use it to capture sound
causes: The headset's microphone uses the HFP (hands-free) profile, with a sample rate and bandwidth far below the A2DP audio channel, so quality is bound to be poor

steps.title: Don't use the Bluetooth mic for capture

steps.title: If you must use it, match at 48kHz and add a sync offset
steps.detail: Set both the system and OBS sample rates to 48kHz; in the Audio Mixer → Advanced Audio Properties, add a manual sync offset to the Bluetooth track to compensate for the fixed delay.

steps.title: If the drift is bad, replace the audio track in post
steps.detail: Record to MKV with two audio tracks (microphone on its own track) and align and replace in post, which is more reliable than toughing it out live.

tips: To tell which profile is active: if Hands-Free appears in Windows sound settings, it's in HFP mode
For streaming, Bluetooth capture is never recommended, since the latency is amplified for viewers

tips: On a limited budget, a single PC plus hardware encoding (NVENC's dedicated encoder) already covers most scenarios; optimize the single PC before considering dual-PC

problems.title: Camera / capture card disconnects and reconnects mid-recording (USB power management)

After unplugging and replugging a USB device, you have to manually reselect it in OBS

Device firmware stability issues under long transfers

steps.title: Disable power saving one by one in Device Manager

steps.title: Plug directly into the motherboard's rear ports
steps.detail: Avoid front-panel ports and hubs; for a high-power capture card, use a separately powered or active hub.

steps.title: Swap the cable / update firmware
steps.detail: A cheap long cable is a killer of signal integrity; if you can, switch to a short brand-name cable, and update the camera / capture card firmware if there's an update.

tips: Before a long recording, do a 30-minute stress test recording to expose most mid-recording disconnect issues early

problems.title: Matching recording frame rate / resolution to the publishing platform's specs
symptoms: A recording that looks crisp locally turns into a blurry mess after uploading to the platform
60fps footage gets compressed by the platform after upload until it looks smeared / stuttery
You don't know what bitrate to export at so it isn't ruined by a second round of compression
causes: After upload each platform transcodes to its own specs, and when the source file's bitrate is below the platform's transcode tier the quality drops irreversibly
Mismatched frame rates (like 59.94 vs 60, or 30 vs 25) cause frame-skipping judder during the platform's transcode
A mismatched portrait / landscape ratio gets force-cropped or given black bars

steps.title: Record at the platform's recommended tier
steps.detail: For 1080p content on Bilibili / Douyin and similar, a source bitrate of at least 10000-16000kbps is recommended (use the upper end for 60fps); the platform's submission guidelines page has the current standard.

steps.title: Use integer standard frame rates
steps.detail: Record at 30 or 60fps, avoiding broadcast rates like 59.94; keep the editing project's frame rate consistent with the recording.

steps.title: Match resolution and aspect ratio
steps.detail: Landscape 1920x1080, portrait 1080x1920; for projects mixing aspect ratios, decide the canvas by the main publishing platform.

steps.title: Don't lower the bitrate when exporting
steps.detail: Rewrap MKV → MP4 to keep the original quality; if you must edit and re-export, the export bitrate should be ≥ the source bitrate.

tips: A source file slightly above the platform's limit is always better than one right at the edge: a second compression only goes down
The Toolbox's parameter preset card includes recommended combinations for common scenarios that you can copy directly

problems.title: Browser Source alert widget blank / frozen: expired widget URL and clearing the cache
symptoms: Follow alerts / donation alerts (Streamlabs, StreamElements, etc.) don't show in the stream or stay blank
Alerts worked before, but after a token reset or switching services they never appeared again
The same widget opens fine in a browser but won't refresh once put into OBS
causes: The alert service's widget URL is regenerated after a token reset / reinstall, invalidating all old URLs
OBS's built-in browser cache is stale, leaving the page on an expired session
The Browser Source has the Refresh when not visible option checked, so it stays on the old state after switching back

steps.title: Verify the URL itself first
steps.detail: Copy the alert service's widget URL into an ordinary browser: if it displays normally the URL is valid and the problem is OBS's cache; if it won't open, go back to the alert dashboard to regenerate the URL and update it in OBS.

steps.title: Refresh the Browser Source
steps.detail: Right-click the source → Refresh (or set a hotkey for Refresh cache); if that still fails, delete and recreate the source and paste the new URL.

steps.title: Clear the built-in browser cache
steps.detail: After fully exiting OBS, delete the %AppData%\obs-studio\obs-browser directory (this only deletes the cache and doesn't affect scenes), then restart OBS.

steps.title: Check hardware acceleration
steps.detail: Settings → Advanced → Video: Browser Hardware Acceleration causes page rendering glitches on some older graphics drivers, so try toggling it to compare.

tips: Resetting the alert service token is the most common cause of a dead URL; after a reset every related Browser Source needs the new URL
Before an important stream, manually refresh each alert source once and trigger it as a test

problems.title: Workarounds when a custom browser dock is stuck and won't refresh

You have to restart OBS to get the panel displaying again

steps.title: Workaround 2: remove and re-add the dock

steps.title: Workaround 3: fall back to an external browser
steps.detail: Put the panel URL in a standalone browser window on a second screen; trade layout integration for stable, controllable refreshing.

steps.title: Follow official progress
steps.detail: This gap has a clear feature request in the official repo and may be filled in a later version; watch the release notes before upgrading.

problems.title: OBS's own hidden overhead: hidden sources left running, duplicate capture, and Browser Source count
symptoms: Even with nothing streaming, game frame rates feel noticeably lower than without OBS
CPU / VRAM usage creeps up with stream duration
The more scenes you have the more it stutters, and deleting a few scenes helps
causes: Sources without Shutdown source when not visible checked: Media Sources and Browser Sources hidden in other scenes are still decoding / rendering
Each Browser Source is a separate render process, so the count directly sets the memory baseline
Display Capture composites the whole desktop into the pipeline, costing more than Game Capture
Duplicate capture: grabbing the same picture with several sources separately

steps.title: Audit the source list
steps.detail: Check each non-persistent source and check Shutdown source when not visible in its properties (OBS 32.x calls it Activate via visibility control); note that a looping video source restarts from the beginning when switched back, so keep such sources persistent.

steps.title: Merge duplicate captures
steps.detail: Keep only one capture source for the same window / display and reuse it across scenes through nested scenes, rather than grabbing a copy in each scene.

steps.title: Limit the number of Browser Sources
steps.detail: Merge widgets that can be merged into one page; for long streams, right-click refresh every 2-3 hours to prevent memory bloat; delete unused alert / chat sources rather than hiding them.

steps.title: Prefer Game Capture
steps.detail: For fullscreen / borderless games use Game Capture, which saves a desktop compositing pass versus Display Capture; if anti-cheat conflicts, fall back to Window / Display Capture.

tips: When you suspect high overhead, run a controlled test: start in Safe Mode (no plugins or scripts) on the same scene, and the difference is the overhead contributed by third parties
Watch the memory trend on the monitoring page; a steady monotonic climb is almost certainly a Browser Source leak

problems.title: Streaming and recording locally at once: GPU budget and degradation order for dual encoding
symptoms: Streaming alone is stable, but checking Record while streaming starts dropped frames / encoding overload
You want to tune recording quality and streaming quality separately and don't know how much extra cost that adds
Game frame rates drop noticeably once dual encoding is on
causes: In Advanced output mode, streaming and recording are two independent encodes, so even on the same graphics card they queue twice (about +10-15% GPU usage)
When software x264 and hardware encoding are mixed, the CPU and GPU each max out and won't yield to each other

steps.title: Stress test before going live
steps.detail: In a demanding scene, run streaming + recording together for 10 minutes and watch the dropped frames in the status bar; exposing it early beats failing live.

steps.title: Pick a low-cost tier for recording
steps.detail: Use hardware encoding + CQP constant quality for recording (like HEVC CQP 20), which is easier than the streaming tier; NVENC's H.264/HEVC/AV1 share the same encoder hardware queue, so watch the total throughput ceiling.

steps.title: Degrade in order
steps.detail: When overloaded, try in turn: lower the recording resolution to 720p → halve the recording frame rate → switch recording to x264 veryfast (give the GPU to streaming) → only then cut streaming parameters.

steps.title: Consider a streaming PC / single high-quality feed
steps.detail: If the budget allows, go with a dual-PC setup; or simply keep a single high-quality output and use the platform's stream recording for playback.

tips: Streaming in H.264 for platform compatibility + recording in high-quality HEVC/AV1 is the most common dual-encoding combo

problems.title: How to choose a preset: x264 presets and NVENC P1~P7 quick reference
symptoms: You're not sure whether to pick x264 veryfast or medium, so you pick slow on a whim and end up with encoding overload
After an NVENC update the presets became P1~P7 and no longer match the old tutorials
You want better quality but fear dropped frames, so you don't dare touch the preset
causes: The slower the x264 preset, the higher the quality, but CPU usage rises non-linearly: it roughly doubles from veryfast to fast, then doubles again at medium
Starting with OBS 30, NVIDIA's new preset system P1 (fastest) ~ P7 (highest quality) replaced the old quality/balanced naming

steps.title: Only three x264 presets are recommended
steps.detail: Start at veryfast for streaming (drop to ultrafast if overloaded); use at most fast for local recording; medium and above are only for offline rendering.

steps.title: Pick NVENC by GPU generation
steps.detail: For RTX 30/40/50 series pick P5 (the quality/performance sweet spot); for GTX 16 / 20 series pick P4; when overloaded, drop the preset by one tier instead of dropping resolution.

steps.title: Matching presets for AMF / QSV
steps.detail: For AMD pick the Quality preset; for Intel QSV start at Balanced, and on machines with newer drivers you can try Quality.

steps.title: How to verify a preset change
steps.detail: Change only one preset tier at a time, run the same scene for 10 minutes, and check whether the encoding lag share in the log analysis drops to zero before deciding the next step.

tips: At the same bitrate, NVENC at P5 generally looks better than x264 veryfast, so prefer hardware encoding if you have an NVIDIA card
Dropping the preset by one tier always hurts the perceived quality less than dropping the resolution by one step

problems.title: Constant quality for recording (CQP / CRF): reference values and when to use them
symptoms: You don't know what recording bitrate to set: too low looks blurry, too high eats disk space
Quality swings between good and bad on static scenes versus intense team fights
You've heard CQP is smarter but don't dare use it
causes: CBR gives every second the same number of bits, so complex scenes are starved while static scenes waste bits
CQP / CRF allocates 'as many bits as needed to maintain the target quality', automatically giving more bits to complex scenes

steps.title: Switch rate control to CQP
steps.detail: Settings → Output → Recording → set Rate Control to CQP (NVENC) / CRF (x264); the lower the value, the higher the quality and the larger the file.

steps.title: Choose the value by encoder
steps.detail: NVENC H.264: CQP 18 is near-lossless, 20 is balanced; for the same look HEVC can go +2; AV1 (40 series+): CQP 22 roughly matches the look of HEVC 18 with files about 30% smaller; x264: CRF 18~23.

steps.title: Raise it if disk space is tight
steps.detail: 1080p60 gameplay at CQP 18 is roughly 15~40GB per hour (varies with content); if space runs short, raise the value by 2 instead of switching to CBR.

steps.title: Don't use CQP for streaming
steps.detail: Platforms require a stable bitrate, so keep CBR for streaming; use CQP only for the local recording path.

tips: Recording footage with CQP avoids the compounding degradation of a second compression pass
Do a 5-minute test recording to estimate the file size, then decide whether to fine-tune the value

problems.title: Live captions / speech-to-text: plugin options when there's no native support
symptoms: You want to add real-time captions to your stream (for deaf viewers / muted viewing), only to find OBS has no native feature
You installed a caption plugin and its recognition latency is high or it doesn't support Chinese
You're worried the caption plugin will eat performance

steps.title: Weigh the cloud engines

steps.title: Performance budget
steps.detail: Local transcription mainly uses CPU / memory and doesn't compete with hardware encoding for GPU; on low-end machines, drop to a smaller model tier or enable it only while speaking.

steps.title: Style and safe area

problems.title: How to choose a streaming server: test by ping and quality, not the automatic default
symptoms: The automatically selected streaming server often drops frames, but switching servers fixes it at once
The node closest to me geographically is worse than one farther away
You don't know which nodes are available or how to test which is better
causes: OBS's 'Auto (Recommended)' usually picks the nearest by location, but ISP routing detours can make a nearby node take the long way around
Node quality fluctuates by time of day, so last night's best isn't necessarily tonight's best

steps.title: List the candidate nodes
steps.detail: Settings → Stream → pick the matching platform under Service; the Server dropdown is the candidate list; Twitch users can also use community speed-test tools to test each one's quality.

steps.title: Shortlist by ping
steps.detail: Run a TCP connection test against the candidate domains (this helper's toolbox provides a probe entry point) and narrow down to the 2~3 with lower RTT; note that low ping is necessary but not sufficient.

steps.title: Verify with real streams
steps.detail: Stream to each shortlisted node for 10 minutes and compare the dropped-frame percentage in the status bar; the one with 0% dropped frames and a stable bitrate is the current best.

steps.title: Re-test periodically
steps.detail: Changes in the network or the platform can shift the best choice, so re-test once a month or whenever dropped frames return; no need to tinker daily.

tips: Ping fluctuates a lot on WiFi, so use a wired connection first to rule out local-network variables before testing nodes
Dropped frames with a sudden bitrate plunge usually mean the node or ISP QoS; switching nodes often fixes it instantly

problems.title: Recording stutters but encoding is fine: disk write speed too low (HDD / full SSD)
symptoms: There's no encoding overload in the log, but the recording stutters every few seconds
The recording gets choppier toward the end (the drive fills up as it writes)
A mechanical hard drive drops frames frequently when recording high-bitrate 1080p60
causes: A mechanical hard drive does only 100~200MB/s sequential writes and much worse random I/O, so it can't sustain high-bitrate recording while multitasking
An SSD filled near capacity, or one whose speed collapses once its cache runs out, slows down mid-recording
The recording drive also handles I/O tasks like downloads / footage sorting, so its bandwidth gets taken

steps.title: Test the disk write speed first
steps.detail: Run a sequential write benchmark on the drive holding your recordings (this helper's toolbox provides a test entry point): the result should be at least planned bitrate / 8000 * 1.5 or more (for example, 20000kbps needs at least about 3.75MB/s of sustained write headroom).

steps.title: Switch to an SSD / NVMe
steps.detail: For high-bitrate recording always start with a SATA SSD; leave mechanical drives for archiving finished files, not as the recording work drive.

steps.title: Leave enough space and TRIM
steps.detail: Keep at least 15% of an SSD free; a nearly full drive is the classic cause of stutter in the second half of a long recording.

steps.title: Stagger I/O
steps.detail: Pause cloud sync, backup, and download tasks while recording; if needed, turn on automatic splitting to give the disk breathing room.

tips: '0% encoding lag but a choppy recording' basically lets you pinpoint the disk path

problems.title: Doubled audio in recordings: two overlapping voices / echo in the file (fine while monitoring live)
symptoms: When playing back the recording, the voice is 'stacked twice, one behind the other', like two people talking at once
While streaming, everything sounds normal through your headphones, but only viewers or the recorded file hear the doubling
Game audio / music also picks up a slight 'chorus-like' delayed layering.
causes: The same audio takes two capture paths into the Audio Mixer: most typically, the microphone is both enabled globally under 'Settings → Audio → Mic' and manually added as an 'Audio Input Capture' source

The 'Monitor and Output' trap: once monitoring is on for the mic, the voice is sent to the playback device, and since 'Desktop Audio' loopbacks the entire playback device, the monitored voice gets recorded a second time - so you can't hear it while recording and only notice it on playback
Camera / capture card sources bring their own mic by default, capturing the audio again alongside your main mic.

steps.title: Classify by what you hear first
steps.detail: Tightly overlapping doubled voices = the same source captured twice; present only in the file and not live = monitor loopback; a progressively widening drift = a sample-rate clock problem (see also av-drift). You can narrow down the direction in about 5 seconds.

steps.title: Clear out duplicate devices
steps.detail: Settings → Audio: disable Mic/Aux 2/3/4 entirely; if the scene already has an 'Audio Input Capture', set the global microphone to disabled so only one path remains.

steps.title: Turn off monitor loopback
steps.detail: Right-click the Audio Mixer → Advanced Audio Properties: set everything except alert browser sources to 'Monitor Off'; if you truly need monitoring, use 'Monitor Only (mute output)'. This one step fixes about 80% of 'streaming is fine, recording has doubled audio' cases.

steps.title: Silence the camera's built-in mic
steps.detail: Double-click the video capture device's properties, set 'Audio Output Mode' to capture only and mute it in the Audio Mixer, or simply disable that device's audio.

tips: Diagnosis trick: solo each source in the Audio Mixer one by one - whichever speaks twice is the culprit
Recording a 30-second test clip to listen back before the real take is the cheapest insurance.

problems.title: Viewers Report Volume Jumping Up and Down: Loudness Consistency
symptoms: Quiet parts are inaudible and shouting parts blast your ears
Loudness is uneven after editing together multiple clips
There's a clear volume gap with a co-host
causes: Only a limiter is used with no compression, so the dynamic range is preserved as-is
Different clips / guests have different input level baselines
There's no quantified target loudness standard; it's all by ear

steps.title: Build a unified chain for each voice source
steps.detail: Build a unified chain for each voice source: gain to set the baseline (peak -12dB) → compression (3:1) → limiting (-1dB) (see au-mic-chain for details)

steps.title: Normalize edit deliverables to a loudness target
steps.detail: Normalize edit deliverables to a loudness target: -14 LUFS (standard for streaming) / -16 LUFS (podcast), done with a single ffmpeg loudnorm command

steps.title: Ask a co-host to speak a 20-second sample first
steps.detail: Ask a co-host to speak a 20-second sample first, then set their gain to match yours based on their peak

steps.title: Route BGM through sidechain ducking
steps.detail: Route BGM through sidechain ducking (au-ducking) to avoid competing with vocals for loudness.

problems.title: Power Plan / Modern Standby Causing Dropped Frames and Encoding Fluctuation
symptoms: On a laptop on battery, the stream framerate periodically dips
When plugged in but on the "Balanced" plan, the encoding time curve shows obvious sawtooth patterns
OBS performance doesn't recover for a long time after sleep/wake
causes: Windows power scheduling aggressively downclocks background processes (EPP / Power Throttling)
Device power state recovers slowly after modern standby wake
Hybrid-GPU laptops make scheduling even more complicated

steps.title: Plug in and set the power plan to "High performance / Ultimate performance" when streaming/recording
steps.detail: Plug in and set the power plan to "High performance / Ultimate performance" when streaming/recording

steps.title: Settings → System → Power
steps.detail: Settings → System → Power: turn off "Lower visual effects in power-saving mode", and exclude OBS from throttling (Graphics settings → obs64.exe → High performance GPU)

steps.title: Streaming on battery is a false need
steps.detail: Streaming on battery is a false need; always stay plugged in

steps.title: If performance is abnormal after wake, restart OBS
steps.detail: If performance is abnormal after wake, restart OBS; restart the machine if necessary.

problems.title: Background Apps Competing: Cloud Sync / Antivirus Scans / System Indexing Drag Down Your Stream
symptoms: Unexplained periodic dropped frames during a stream, matching the timing of OneDrive/iCloud sync or Windows Defender scans
Recording write speed keeps fluctuating
It's especially laggy within half an hour of boot
causes: IO contention when cloud sync and recording write to the same disk
Antivirus real-time scanning hooks the writes of large recording files
The Windows Search indexer reads the disk aggressively when it hits the recording directory

steps.title: Pause cloud sync while recording/streaming
steps.detail: Pause cloud sync while recording/streaming (the OneDrive Pause for 2 hours button), or move the recording directory out of sync scope

steps.title: Add the OBS and recording directories to your antivirus exclusion list
steps.detail: Add the OBS and recording directories to your antivirus exclusion list

steps.title: Turn off Windows Search indexing for the recording directory
steps.detail: Turn off Windows Search indexing for the recording directory (folder Properties → Advanced)

steps.title: Use Resource Monitor to confirm the disk queue length during a stream is close to 0, which is healthy
steps.detail: Use Resource Monitor to confirm the disk queue length during a stream is close to 0, which is healthy.

problems.title: Home Network Bandwidth Contention: Family Streaming / Downloads Max Out Your Upload
symptoms: Dropped frames right on schedule at evening peak hours, with no issues during the day
The stream degrades immediately when someone at home watches 4K streaming / hammers cloud drives
A wired speed test is fine, but it collapses as soon as you stream
causes: Home upload is only 30~50Mbps to begin with, so a single device doing cloud backup can eat it all
The router doesn't do QoS, so stream traffic and download traffic compete equally
On WiFi, multiple devices competing for airtime make it worse

steps.title: Measure your actual home upload
steps.detail: Measure your actual home upload (speedtest) and reserve stream bitrate ×1.3 of headroom for streaming

steps.title: Enable QoS / per-device rate limiting on the router
steps.detail: Enable QoS / per-device rate limiting on the router, set the streaming PC to the highest priority, and limit the upload of other devices

steps.title: Keep the streaming PC wired
steps.detail: Keep the streaming PC wired; schedule other high-traffic tasks (backup/downloads) for non-streaming hours

steps.title: For stubborn congestion, consider an ISP upload upgrade or a second line
steps.detail: For stubborn congestion, consider an ISP upload upgrade or a second line (streaming on a separate broadband connection).

problems.title: Mobile Viewing Gets Cropped: Planning a Safe Area for Portrait / Landscape
symptoms: The composition is perfect on the PC, but people on both sides get cut off when viewed in portrait on a phone
Chat / like bubbles cover the subtitles and faces
Platform UI (follow button, progress bar) covers key information
causes: The portrait client zooms and crops landscape content to fill
Platform floating controls occupy the four corners and the lower third of the frame
Subtitles sit below the bottom edge of the safe area

steps.title: For portrait streaming, use a 1080×1920 canvas to make native portrait content
steps.detail: For portrait streaming, use a 1080×1920 canvas to make native portrait content (st-vertical); don't expect to convert landscape to portrait

steps.title: Key information in landscape content
steps.detail: Keep the key information in landscape content (faces, subtitles, Logo) within the central 4:3 area, leaving ~10% buffer on each side

steps.title: Place subtitles in the 70%~85% range of the frame height
steps.detail: Place subtitles in the 70%~85% range of the frame height, avoiding the dense chat area and the platform progress bar

steps.title: Preview on a real phone for 5 minutes before finalizing the composition

problems.title: VTuber Face Tracking Pipeline: Coordinating Tracking Software with OBS and Performance
symptoms: VSeeFace/PrprLive tracking stutters and expressions lag
After capturing the face-tracking window into OBS, the background becomes an opaque white block
Running face tracking + a game at the same time blows up the GPU
causes: Face-tracking inference (especially camera-based setups) keeps using CPU/GPU
A transparent background needs Spout2 (NVIDIA/Windows) or Syphon (macOS) to pass through; Window Capture can't get alpha
Too many polygons in the model cause dropped frames on low-end machines

steps.title: Transmission method
steps.detail: Transmission method: on Windows, use the Spout2 plugin to directly receive the alpha-channel output of the face-tracking software; on macOS, use Syphon

steps.title: If that's not possible, use a chroma key to remove a solid background
steps.detail: If that's not possible, use a chroma key to remove a solid background (cf-chroma); slightly less precise but universal

steps.title: Lower the sampling rate / simplify the model tier in the face-tracking software
steps.detail: Lower the sampling rate / simplify the model tier in the face-tracking software, and leave the GPU budget for the game and encoding

steps.title: iPhone face tracking
steps.detail: iPhone face tracking (ARKit) is the most accurate and doesn't use PC processing power; it's worth having a cable for it.

problems.title: TikTok LIVE Studio / Streaming Abroad: Eligibility and OBS Integration
symptoms: Can't find TikTok's stream key and unsure whether OBS can be used
The LIVE Studio client and OBS overlap in features, unsure which to pick
A region restriction prompt appears after going live
causes: TikTok applies a follower threshold (historically ≥1000 followers) and region eligibility for direct OBS streaming; when the criteria aren't met, the dashboard doesn't show the stream key entry
LIVE Studio is the official client with built-in beauty filters / gift interaction, but it's less flexible than OBS

steps.title: Eligible users in the TikTok LIVE dashboard
steps.detail: Eligible users get the RTMP server and key in the TikTok LIVE dashboard (or LIVE Studio settings), then choose "Custom" for the service in OBS and enter them

steps.title: If not eligible, you can only use LIVE Studio or stream from your phone to build up eligibility
steps.detail: If not eligible, you can only use LIVE Studio or stream from your phone to build up eligibility

steps.title: Make sure your account's registration region matches your actual IP region
steps.detail: Make sure your account's registration region matches your actual IP region; streaming across borders easily triggers risk controls

steps.title: Use a 1080×1920 canvas for portrait streaming
steps.detail: Use a 1080×1920 canvas for portrait streaming (st-vertical); landscape content will be cropped.

problems.title: Auto-Configuration Wizard Settings Don't Fit: When to Trust It, When to Override It
symptoms: After "optimizing" with the wizard, the stream is blurrier / starts dropping frames
The bitrate the wizard gives is far below the platform's recommended value
The resolution is automatically dropped to 720p, which feels unsatisfying
causes: The wizard makes conservative decisions based on a one-off bandwidth test and estimated framerate; a momentary low speed reading makes it conservative across the board
It doesn't understand contexts like "game load fluctuation" or "platform transcoding tiers"

steps.title: Treat the wizard's result as a starting point, not the end
steps.detail: Treat the wizard's result as a starting point, not the end: run one session first, then check the dropped frames / encoding lag data in the log analyzer

steps.title: Manually verify the bitrate against the enc-bitrate-guide cheat sheet
steps.detail: Manually verify the bitrate against the enc-bitrate-guide cheat sheet; it can usually be raised 20%~50%

steps.title: Set resolution/framerate by content type
steps.detail: Set resolution/framerate by content type (for competitive games, 1080p60 over 1440p30)

steps.title: Change only one thing at a time and re-test
steps.detail: Change only one thing at a time and re-test, to avoid changing multiple things at once and being unable to attribute the effect.
